goal: Confirm systemd-run --user --scope --collect places the child in a cgroup independent of the parent, surviving both a sibling unit restart and a kill -9 of the launching process; confirm the setsid+double-fork fallback behavior when no D-Bus user session is present.
host: dev.tjstkm.net (this box) — Ubuntu, home-manager-managed palmux2 host, systemd --user session present (systemd 255.4-1ubuntu8.16)
environment_notes: The ambient Bash tool shell for this agent session runs INSIDE the production host palmux2's own cgroup (/system.slice/palmux2.service) — confirmed via `cat /proc/self/cgroup`. This is a useful real-world proxy for 'a process whose parent-ish ancestry is palmux2'. The ambient shell did NOT have XDG_RUNTIME_DIR / DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS set by default (systemctl --user status failed with 'Failed to connect to bus: No medium found') even though the user's systemd --user manager and D-Bus session socket both exist at /run/user/1000. Exporting XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus fixed this. This is an environment-derivation detail palmux2's real spawn path must handle (env may need to be set explicitly rather than assumed inherited) — noted as an implementation concern for the launcher, not a spike failure.
cgroup_evidence: Spawned via: setsid bash -c "exec systemd-run --user --scope --collect --unit spike-scope-<rand> -- /tmp/spike_child_proc.sh" (a disposable 'fake launcher' safe to kill).
Real child PID (leader inside the scope, shown by `systemctl --user status spike-scope-<rand>.scope`): cgroup = /user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/spike-scope-<rand>.scope
The scope child's PPID was 1 (reparented to init) and SID == its own PID (new session) — fully detached from any parent shell.

CORRECTION (found during S3f2658-1 implementation, superseding the initial pass's mechanism claim below): `systemd-run --user --scope` does NOT self-detach. Re-measured directly with `timeout 8 systemd-run --user --scope --collect --unit X -- sleep 30 </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1`: this blocked for the FULL 8s (exit 124), and killing the outer systemd-run process (via `timeout`'s SIGTERM) also tore down the scope (`systemctl --user status` reported the unit 'could not be found' afterward). A second direct test backgrounding `systemd-run --user --scope --collect --unit Y -- sleep 60 &` and polling `kill -0 $!` once per second for 8s showed the systemd-run process ITSELF staying alive the whole time (it is a synchronous foreground wrapper that relays stdio and forwards signals to the child, matching documented systemd-run --scope behavior — akin to `tini`/`dumb-init`). The reason the original spike's 'fake launcher' PID (the setsid-bash-turned-systemd-run process) appeared to have already exited when checked from a LATER, separate shell command is that this agent's tool harness reaps backgrounded processes left over from a completed command; `setsid` only creates a new session (immune to SIGHUP) and does not protect against that reaping, exactly as already documented below for the setsid-fallback cgroup caveat. What actually escapes the cgroup is the process systemd-run FORKS to exec the target (migrated into the new scope's cgroup by systemd via the D-Bus transient-unit call within tens of milliseconds) — NOT systemd-run's own top-level pid, which never migrates. Because the forked+migrated target does not depend on systemd-run's stdio relay for anything once running (in our real design it is `palmux ptyhost`, which owns its own PTY/socket independently), it is unaffected by systemd-run's own process later dying by any means (explicit kill, or a cgroup-wide teardown of whatever cgroup systemd-run's own top-level pid was started in) — Linux does not cascade-kill children when a parent dies. CONCLUSION UNCHANGED (cgroup escape genuinely works, confirmed independently by SURVIVAL-A/B below against the real production scenario), but the IMPLEMENTATION must not synchronously wait() for systemd-run (that would block palmux2 for the whole agent session) — it must start it and immediately release its process handle (fire-and-forget), exactly like the setsid fallback. internal/ptyhost/launch.go's RunSystemdScope was corrected to Start()+Process.Release() instead of Run() as a direct result of this finding; see TestLaunch_RealHost_DetachesFromTestProcess for the passing real-host regression test of the corrected behavior.
survival_a_evidence: Created a transient service unit `palmux2-spiketest.service` (systemd-run --user --collect --unit palmux2-spiketest -- <fake_palmux2.sh>) whose own script spawns the systemd-run --scope child from WITHIN its own process tree (closest analogue to palmux2 spawning a ptyhost). Captured scope child pid, then ran `systemctl --user restart palmux2-spiketest.service`. After restart, `MainPID` of the service changed (new process), but `kill -0 <scope-child-pid>` succeeded and the scope child's cgroup was unchanged (/user.slice/.../app.slice/spike-scope2-<id>.scope). Logged SURVIVAL-A: PASS.
survival_b_evidence: Took the current MainPID of palmux2-spiketest.service and ran `kill -9 <pid>`. `systemctl --user show` then reported ActiveState=inactive, Result=success, MainPID=0 (the fake-palmux2 process was gone). The scope child (same PID as before) still answered `kill -0` and its cgroup was still the isolated scope. Logged SURVIVAL-B: PASS.
setsid_fallback_evidence: Ran `env -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS bash -c 'systemd-run --user --scope --collect --unit fallback-test-probe -- true'` to simulate a no-D-Bus environment: systemd-run exited 1 ('Failed to connect to bus: No medium found') — confirms a runtime probe (try systemd-run, check exit code) reliably detects unavailability. Then ran the actual fallback path: `setsid /tmp/spike_child2.sh </dev/null >log 2>&1 & disown` from within the no-D-Bus env. The resulting process (after the wrapper script's `exec sleep 300`) had PPID=1 (reparented to init, proving detach from the launching shell) and SID equal to its own PID (new session, no controlling terminal) — this IS a genuine detach.
setsid_fallback_cgroup_caveat: IMPORTANT (matches ADR-0003's predicted alternative-tradeoff exactly): the setsid-detached process's cgroup remained /system.slice/palmux2.service — i.e. setsid does NOT escape the systemd cgroup by itself. Under a systemd-managed palmux2 (KillMode=cgroup, the systemd default), a `systemctl --user restart`/`stop` of palmux2 would still SIGKILL a setsid-only-detached ptyhost because it never left palmux2's cgroup. This confirms the design's stated scope: the setsid fallback path is a correct DETACH mechanism (process, session, controlling-terminal independence) but is only a genuine SURVIVAL mechanism in non-systemd deployments (e.g. `make serve` / `make dev`, which are not run under a systemd unit at all and so never receive a cgroup-wide kill signal in the first place). In a systemd-managed production host with no D-Bus user session (a degenerate/misconfigured case ADR-0003 does not claim to solve), setsid fallback provides orphan-safety (no zombie, no double-fork leak) but not restart-survival — this is accepted as an explicit, documented gap, not silently glossed over.
notes: Both production classes referenced in the design (Ubuntu/home-manager and the NixOS palmuxOS appliance) run palmux2 as a systemd --user (home-manager) or systemd system (NixOS module, per CLAUDE.md Sb14caa) unit with a live D-Bus user session — this spike's host (Ubuntu/home-manager) is the direct analogue for the home-manager class. The NixOS-appliance class is asserted equivalent per ADR-0003 (D-Bus user session present in both) but a live NixOS run is deferred, consistent with the plan's spike scope (real NixOS run happens at the SURVIVAL AC / later milestone smoke, not in this foundational spike).
--collect was used throughout: no failed-state scope/service units were left behind after the child exited (confirmed via `systemctl --user list-units` showing 0 matching units after cleanup).

Conclusion for implementation: the launcher (internal/ptyhost/launch.go) MUST runtime-probe systemd-run (attempt the real launch; a non-zero exit / exec error triggers fallback) rather than a static environment flag, exactly as ADR-0003 specifies. It should also explicitly propagate/derive XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS (falling back to /run/user/<uid>/bus when unset) since the ambient environment cannot be assumed to already export them.

All spike-created transient units, temp scripts, and processes were cleaned up (kill -9 on leftover PIDs + systemctl --user reset-failed + rm of /tmp/spike_*). No production palmux2 process was touched at any point (per forbidden-list constraint).
verdict: PASS — systemd-run --user --scope --collect path confirmed to fully isolate the child's cgroup and survive both sibling-unit restart and kill -9 of the launching process (SURVIVAL-A and SURVIVAL-B both PASS on this real systemd host). setsid+double-fork fallback confirmed to genuinely detach (PPID=1, new session) but, as ADR-0003 anticipates, does not escape an existing systemd cgroup — its survival guarantee is scoped to non-systemd (dev rig) deployments. Proceeding with Wave 1 implementation per ADR-0003 as written. MECHANISM CORRECTION (see cgroup_evidence): systemd-run --scope is a synchronous foreground wrapper, not self-detaching — the launcher must Start()+Release() (fire-and-forget) rather than Run() (wait). This does not change the verdict (cgroup escape still holds, re-verified by TestLaunch_RealHost_DetachesFromTestProcess and by SURVIVAL-A/B being measured against the real scenario all along), only the correct Go implementation shape.
